art.subject: Booted Eagle (Hieraaetus pennatus), adult pale morph: head buff-brown with a darker streaked crown; upperparts dark brown with a broad pale buff band across the upperwing coverts and pale buff uppertail coverts forming a U at the base of the tail; small white patches where the forewing meets the body; underparts and underwing coverts creamy white, lightly streaked on the breast, contrasting with blackish flight feathers; inner primaries paler, forming a pale wedge; tail grey-brown and unbarred. Bill dark grey with a yellow cere; legs feathered to the toes, feet yellow.
art.pose: soaring over a wooded hillside, seen from below
art.scene: Korean wooded hills and open valley during autumn migration under a clear sky; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small eagle, about the size of an Eastern Buzzard, compact with a small head and a long, square-ended tail. Bill short and hooked, shorter than the head. Legs feathered to the toes, giving the booted look. In flight long, rather narrow, parallel-edged wings with well-spread primary fingers, held flat or with the hand slightly lowered; the tail is often fanned when soaring.
avoid: Do not paint a barred tail or dark wrist patches like a buzzard; the tail is plain and the underwing coverts uniformly pale.
Do not paint a dark band across the underwing coverts (Bonelli's Eagle); on this pale morph the coverts are creamy white.
Do not forget the pale band across the upperwing coverts and the pale U on the uppertail coverts.
Do not paint bare yellow legs; the legs are feathered.
